newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi offer proceeding despite pitfalls.
newsitem.headline: Leumi offer proceeding despite pitfalls.

text.p: MI Holdings, the government company charged with selling Israel's state-owned banks, is proceeding with a secondary offering in Bank Leumi despite potential pitfalls, MI Holdings chairman said on Monday.
"We are working on selling the shares in Bank Leumi. I hope that in May we will make a secondary offering," Chairman Uzi Steinberg told Reuters.

He said current plans call for floating another 10-15 percent of Leumi, Israel's second-largest bank, on top of the 18 percent already traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE). The remainder is owned by the government.
At Leumi's current market valuation, the offering could be worth up to $410 million.
The offering would come on the heels of another big issue for 17 percent of Israel Discount Bank, which is now expected to go ahead in April.

The Discount offering, which would be for about $175 million, was to take place last month but delayed after the Securities Authority asked to see more detailed information on its fourth-quarter debt provision.

In addition, the Israeli share market has seen the glow on a rally that began in November dim recently. The TASE's Mishtanim index of top 100 shares peaked on February 18 at 270.87 and has since declined 5.5 percent amid falling volume.
But Steinberg said he is not concerned about either problem, saying MI Holdings could not alter plans according to every change in the market's direction.
"Our planning is going forward without any connection to the stock market....The market was excellent two months ago and now it is so-so. But you need time to prepare an offering," he said.

Moshe Leon, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's economic adviser, said he is pushing to move ahead quickly to sell a controlling stake in Leumi by tender. Last week, the government announced it was re-opening bidding for Bank Hapoalim.
Leon said he wanted the Leumi sale process to start "a little later than Hapoalim's...later this year."
That would give MI Holdings the task of selling Israel's two biggest banks simultaneously after two years of little movement towards divesting state holdings.

Steinberg said it was premature to discuss selling a controlling stake in Leumi simultaneouly with a sale in Bank Hapoalim. He said the issue should be raised only when the Hapoalim tender is further advanced.

The government has published a notice asking potential bidders for Hapoalim to present proposals by April 18 and has said it plans to complete the sale of between 25 percent and 69.3 percent by mid-August.

The government decided to move forward with the Hapoalim tender, Steinberg said, because there are two serious groups interested in the bank. Without any advance notice of serious interest there is "no reason to publish a tender like this," he said regarding Leumi.

Neither Leon nor Steinberg would comment on newspaper reports that Edmond Safra, who controls Republic New York Corp, has expressed renewed interest in Leumi. Safra dropped out of a tender for Leumi in 1995.
